newsitem.title: USA: Kodak faces U.S. pricing pressure-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Kodak faces U.S. pricing pressure-analyst.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co faces severe pricing pressure in the U.S. film industry from Fuji Photo Film Co, a Prudential Securities analyst said, citing retail sales data from Information Resources Inc and industry insiders.
Kodak shares were down 4-3/8 to 79-1/2 in late afternoon trade.
According to Prudential analyst Alexander Henderson, a pricing war is brewing in the U.S. film industry because "Fuji is being very agressive in its pricing against Kodak and private labels."
Fuji is pricing at a level that is pressuring private labels, which are typically priced between 40.0-50.0 percent below brand-name film, Henderson said.

That could portend a "real pricing war," Henderson said, adding that he estimates Kodak may have lost between three and four percentage points of U.S. market share in the 35 millimeter market so far this year to Fuji.
"This is a yellow flag on Kodak," Henderson said. "We're very concerned."
Other analyst also expressed concern about Kodak's shares.
Salamon Brothers analyst Jonathan Rosenzweig said in a research note that he has "received mixed signals regarding Kodak's near-term outlook in the consumer area.
